items.text: Michael Douglas is going to the Karlovy Vary Film Festival to show a new version of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest. This is a special event at the festival because the movie is 50 years old. Douglas helped make the film and will speak before the show. He will come with another producer , Paul Zaentz, and people from the family of the director, Miloš Forman. The movie won five big Oscars and is very famous. It was directed by Forman, who is from the Czech Republic. Douglas also won an Oscar for this film. The film festival takes place in a beautiful town. It has a long history with the movie and its team. Douglas and others got the Crystal Globe prize there for their work in movies. Difficult words: festival (a special event with many shows), producer (a person who helps make a movie), prize (a reward for good work). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Michael Douglas goes to the Karlovy Vary Film Festival . He shows a new version of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest. The movie is now 50 years old. Douglas helps make this movie. He comes with Paul Zaentz and the family of the director, Miloš Forman. The movie wins many big prizes . It is very famous. The director, Forman, is from the Czech Republic. Douglas also wins a big prize for this movie. The festival takes place in a nice town. Douglas and others get a prize called the Crystal Globe there. Difficult words: festival (a special event with many shows), version (a form of something), prize (a reward for good work). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A US judge has dismissed Justin Baldoni’s 400-million-dollar defamation lawsuit against Blake Lively. Baldoni claimed Lively wrongly accused him of sexual harassment during the filming of It Ends with Us. However, the judge said Lively’s complaint to a California agency was privileged, meaning it was legally protected. The judge also dismissed Baldoni’s 250-million-dollar lawsuit against The New York Times, which had reported on the conflict. The judge said Baldoni didn’t give enough facts to support the claim that Lively and others tried to ruin his reputation on purpose . He may still file another lawsuit based on their contract. Meanwhile, Lively’s lawsuit against Baldoni continues. She is asking for more damages , and a trial is going to take place in 2026. Lively’s lawyers called the dismissal a victory. They said Baldoni’s lawsuit was a dishonest way to attack her. The Times also defended its reporting, saying the court supported the freedom of the press to report important stories. Difficult words: defamation (saying something false that harms someone’s reputation), on purpose (intentionally), damages (money a person asks for after being harmed). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A judge in the US stopped Justin Baldoni’s 400-million-dollar lawsuit against Blake Lively. Baldoni said Lively lied about him harassing her during filming. He also sued The New York Times, but the judge stopped that case, too. The judge said Baldoni didn’t show enough facts to prove Lively and others tried to hurt his name. He can try a smaller case about a contract. Lively is still suing Baldoni, and their court trial will happen in 2026. Lively’s lawyers said they were happy. They said Baldoni’s lawsuit was not honest. The Times said the judge showed that reporters can safely tell important news stories. Difficult words: lawsuit (a legal case in court), harass (to treat someone badly again and again), prove (to show that something exists or is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A judge says Justin Baldoni cannot continue his big court case against Blake Lively. Baldoni says Lively says bad things about him during a movie. But the judge says that this is okay. The judge also stops Baldoni’s case against a newspaper. The judge says Baldoni does not have enough information that something bad happens. He says that Baldoni can start a smaller court case. Lively has her case. She wants money. They are going to court again in 2026. Lively’s lawyers are happy. They say that Baldoni’s court case is not real. The newspaper says they only tell a news story, and the judge thinks the same. Difficult words: continue (to keep doing something), case (a problem or story in court), lawyer (a person who helps you in court). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chiquita, a large American banana company, plans to stop all work in Panama and make all its workers redundant . The decision comes after long protests over new pension laws. Earlier in May, the company had already laid off around 5,000 workers after strikes disrupted banana production. Although a court said the strike was illegal, the protests continued. Now, Chiquita says it will close operations in the region and has already moved key staff to Costa Rica. The president of Panama says this is a big problem for the country’s economy, especially for regions that depend on banana farming. The loss of 7,000 jobs could cause major problems like poverty, food shortages, and school closures. Many people now fear that the company will leave Panama completely. Government officials hope that dialogue can still help resolve the issue. However, they say workers must also be willing to talk. If not, the region may face more poverty and fewer job opportunities in the future. Difficult words: redundant (losing a job because the company no longer needs it), lay off (to end a worker’s job, usually because there is not enough work to do), dialogue (talking to find a solution). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Chiquita is a big banana company from the US. It wants to stop working in Panama and will let go of all its workers. In May, it already let go of 5,000 workers. The workers were unhappy about new pension laws and started a strike. The court said the strike was illegal, but it still went on . Panama’s president says this is very bad for the country. Many people work on banana farms, and if the farms close, 7,000 people will lose their jobs. This will cause problems like less food and fuel, and many schools may close. The government hopes to find a solution . They want to talk with the workers and the company, but the workers don’t want to talk. If they don’t find a way, life will be harder for many people. Difficult words: pension (money people get after they stop working), go on (to continue), solution (a way to fix a problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chiquita is a big banana company. It works in Panama. Now, it wants to stop all work in the country. The company wants to say goodbye to all workers. The workers do not like the new law. They stop working. There is a strike . Chiquita says that the strike is not okay. But the workers still do not work. The president of Panama says that the problem is big. Many people in one area grow bananas. If Chiquita stops, many people will have no job. The government wants to talk. The workers must talk too. If not, people will have no money or food. Difficult words: strike (when people stop working to show that they are not happy), government (the people who run a country).

JAWS @ 50: THE DEFINITIVE INSIDE STORY is the official documentary about the legendary film Jaws, released 50 years ago. It includes interviews with director Steven Spielberg, Hollywood filmmakers, shark experts, and conservationists. The film tells the story of how Peter Benchley’s bestselling book became a blockbuster movie that changed Hollywood. Rare behind-the-scenes footage shows how the production struggled with real ocean filming, technical failures, and intense stress. The shark didn’t work most of the time, the movie was 100 days behind schedule, and Spielberg feared he would be fired. But the hard work paid off . Jaws became the first summer blockbuster, influenced generations of filmmakers, and started important conversations about shark protection. Spielberg said making Jaws changed his life. The film became a pop culture phenomenon and helped shape the modern movie industry. Despite better technology today, many agree no film has matched its impact. What was once expected to end Spielberg’s career launched it. Difficult words: legendary (very famous and admired for a long time), pay off (to get a good result after hard work or problems), pop culture phenomenon (something in movies, music, or media that becomes very popular and important to many people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

JAWS @ 50 is a new film about the famous movie Jaws. It shows how filmmakers made the movie 50 years ago. Director Steven Spielberg and others talk about what happened behind the scenes . The movie was hard to make. They filmed in the ocean, the shark often didn’t work, and they were late finishing. Spielberg was scared he might lose his job. In the end, Jaws became a big hit and started the idea of the summer blockbuster . It also helped people care more about sharks. Experts, scientists, and movie makers all share their memories. Spielberg says Jaws changed his life. Even though there are new shark movies with computer effects, Jaws is still the best to many people. Difficult words: behind the scenes (what happens during filming that people don’t see), hit (a movie or song which becomes very popular), blockbuster (a very popular movie). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

JAWS @ 50 is a movie about how filmmakers make the old film Jaws. It comes out 50 years ago. Steven Spielberg is the director . When they make the movie, the shark does not work well. They film in the ocean for five months. It is very hard. People are tired and scared . But in the end, the movie is a big hit . It makes many people want to watch movies in the summer. It also helps people care about sharks. Now, people still love Jaws. Even with new shark movies, many people say that this one is the best. Spielberg says making Jaws changes his life. Difficult words: director (the boss of making a movie), scared (afraid, worried), h it (a popular movie or song). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kilmar García, a man wrongly deported to El Salvador in March, is now back in the US and has been indicted . The US attorney general confirmed that García faces two federal charges: conspiracy to transport undocumented migrants and unlawful transportation of them. Authorities believe García helped smuggle migrants from Central America into the US over nine years. Though undocumented himself, García had a court order blocking his deportation because he argued he faced danger in El Salvador. His case drew political attention, reaching the Supreme Court, which ruled he must return to the US to get due process . A past traffic stop in Tennessee raised suspicions of human trafficking, but no charges were made at the time. García’s family denies the claims, saying he worked in construction. Despite that, the federal indictment now links him to about 100 smuggling trips. Once his legal case ends, he is expected to be deported again. Difficult words: indicted (formally charged), conspiracy (a secret plan to do something illegal), due process (fair legal treatment). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man named Kilmar García was deported to El Salvador in March, but it was a mistake. Now, he is back in the US and faces two criminal charges. The government says García made about 100 trips to smuggle people from Central America to the US for many years. Although a court said he could be in danger in El Salvador, he was deported. His story became very important, and the US top court said he must return to have a fair trial . He also had a speeding stop where police thought he was helping with human trafficking, but they didn’t arrest him. His family says he only worked in construction. Difficult words: deported (sent back to another country), smuggle (to move things or people illegally into or out of a country), trial (a formal meeting in a court). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kilmar García must leave the US and go back to El Salvador. It happens in March, but it is a mistake . He is now back in the US. The police say he helps bring people into the US without official papers. He makes around 100 trips to Central America. He is now in trouble and may go to court . A long time ago, a judge says García can stay in the US because El Salvador is not safe for him. But they send him anyway. Later, the court says he must come back to have a fair trial . García’s family says he does nothing wrong. He only works in building houses. Difficult words: mistake (something wrong), court (a place where meetings with a judge happen), fair trial (a chance to speak to a judge and explain what you do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many Japanese people have been lining up at stores to purchase rice at a reduced price, which the government released. Due to extreme weather and other reasons, rice prices in Japan have doubled since last year. As a response, the government decided to release emergency rice stockpiles directly to retailers for half the usual price. This policy change is aimed at helping consumers and easing pressure before upcoming elections. Shoppers are allowed to buy only one bag per household, but long queues have still formed, showing how serious the situation has become. Farm Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said that the government is ready to release even more stockpiled rice if necessary. He also suggested buying back rice from wholesalers to increase supply and lower prices further. He warned that if local prices stay too high, stores might fill their shelves with more imported rice instead. Imports of foreign rice have already increased sharply despite high tariffs. More rice is expected to be produced in Japan this year. Difficult words: line up (to stand in a row), stockpile (a large stored supply of something), retailer (a store that sells products to customers). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many people in Japan now wait in long lines to buy cheap rice. The government started selling emergency rice in shops to help with the high prices. Rice now costs about twice as much as last year, while cheap rice sells for about half the usual price. Shoppers can only buy one bag each, but many still come early and wait. The farm minister says the government can give more rice if needed. He also wants to buy back rice from some sellers to help bring more rice to stores. He is worried that high prices will make stores sell more rice from other countries. Rice imports are going up. Even with extra taxes, people buy more foreign rice because it is cheaper. Japan hopes to grow more rice this year. Difficult words: import (things for sale from another country), extra (more than usual), foreign (from or in another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Japan, many people go to stores to buy cheap rice. The government gives this rice to help with high prices. One bag costs less than usual. Each person can take only one bag. Still, many people wait in line. The rice price goes up. The farm minister says that the government can give more rice. He also wants to get rice from sellers to help people. He says that shops may sell rice from other countries if the price stays high. People also buy rice from other countries. It is cheaper, even with extra cost. Japan wants to grow more rice this year. Difficult words: government (the group of people who lead a country), farm minister (a top person who takes care of farming, food, and growing things on land), extra (more than usual). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two people died, and hundreds were arrested in France after Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) won the Champions League. Following the victory over Inter Milan, riots broke out in several cities. Police reported 491 arrests in Paris alone and over 60 more across the country. Cars were set on fire, fireworks were used, and fights happened between supporters and police. A 17-year-old was stabbed in Dax, and a 23-year-old man died in Paris after a scooter accident. Many people were hurt, including police officers, firefighters, and fans. One officer in Normandy was placed in a coma after a firework accident. Still, most PSG fans celebrated peacefully, and Sunday’s parade in Paris passed without major problems. PSG condemned the violence and said true fans show respect. The events led to political arguments. Some politicians blamed lawless groups, while others criticized the police. Riot police used tear gas and arrested several people. In another city, a car accident injured a family. Meanwhile, fans also caused disruptions in Munich before the game. Difficult words: coma (a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness), condemn (to strongly say something is wrong), lawless (illegal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

After PSG won the Champions League over Inter Milan, there was trouble in France. People went to the streets to celebrate, but many fights started. The police arrested 491 people in Paris and more in other places. Two people died, one was a teenager, and one was riding a scooter. Fireworks and fires caused many problems. A police officer was badly hurt by a firework. Still, most fans were peaceful . On Sunday, PSG had a parade, and it was calm. The club said the bad actions were not from real fans. Some politicians were angry. One said bad people made the streets unsafe. Others said the police were too strong. In Munich, PSG and Inter fans fought at a train station. In another city, a car hit people during a party. Difficult words: peaceful (calm), parade (a line of people celebrating in the street). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

PSG wins the Champions League on Saturday. They beat Inter Milan. After the game, some people in France are happy. But some people make problems. People start fires and make noise. Some people fight with the police. Police arrest many people. Two people die. One boy dies after a knife attack. One man has an accident on a scooter. A police officer is hurt , too. But many fans are nice and happy. PSG says that fighting is bad. They want fans to be kind . Some politicians are angry. They say that the police are too strong. In another place, a car hits people. Four people are hurt. Difficult words: arrest (when the police take someone because they do something wrong), hurt (to feel pain or have an injury), kind (nice and caring to others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Anime, or Japanese animation, has become one of the fastest-growing areas in global entertainment. At the center of this boom is Crunchyroll, a streaming platform that started small but now serves over 17 million subscribers across 200 countries. It brings anime to fans around the world by licensing shows from Japanese creators and offering subtitled and dubbed versions in several languages. Crunchyroll’s biggest success is Solo Leveling, a series inspired by video games, which became a top hit in many regions. The growing interest in anime has led other major platforms, such as Netflix, to join the competition. Overseas interest in anime has now become larger than the market inside Japan. Crunchyroll currently holds about 75% of Japan’s anime titles on its service. Crunchyroll is not only active in television. It is also behind many of the top anime films in US box office history, including Demon Slayer, which broke long-standing records. Fans can also buy merchandise , play games, or enjoy anime in cinemas. Difficult words: dub (to replace original voices in a film with voices in another language), box office (the place in a cinema or theatre where tickets are sold), merchandise (products related to a show, like toys or T-shirts). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Anime is Japanese animation, and it is becoming very popular around the world. Crunchyroll is a company that shows anime online. It started small but now has more than 17 million users in 200 countries. It works with Japanese artists and shows their programs in many languages. One of Crunchyroll’s most popular anime shows is Solo Leveling, which is about games and getting stronger. Many fans like this kind of story. Other companies like Netflix also want to show anime, and now more people outside Japan watch anime than people in Japan. Crunchyroll also helps make anime movies. One very big hit is Demon Slayer. It made more money than any other anime movie before. Crunchyroll also lets fans buy merchandise , play games, or enjoy anime in cinemas. Difficult words: animation (moving images in movies), merchandise (products about a show, like toys or T-shirts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Anime is a kind of Japanese cartoon . It is very fun. Many people in the world like it. A company called Crunchyroll shows anime. It is on the Internet. Many people use it in many countries. Crunchyroll has a show called Solo Leveling. It is a game story. The person in the show gets stronger. Many people like it. Another company is Netflix. It also shows anime. A lot of people outside Japan watch anime these days. Crunchyroll also helps with anime movies. One big movie is Demon Slayer. Many people watch it. Crunchyroll also sells toys and games. People can play, watch, and buy things about anime. Difficult words: cartoon (a fun show with drawings), toy (a thing to play with). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the early 1990s, Bosnia went through a terrible war after the breakup of Yugoslavia. The capital, Sarajevo, was under siege for nearly four years. Thousands of people died from sniper attacks, bombs, and starvation. Life was extremely dangerous. People could be shot just for walking down the street or trying to find food or water. A man named John Jordan, an American and ex-Marine, went to Sarajevo to help. He brought clothes and supplies for firefighters and risked his life many times. In 2007, he testified in court and said that wealthy foreigners traveled to Sarajevo to shoot civilians for fun. He called them tourist shooters. According to Jordan, these people were from countries like Italy, the US, Canada, and Russia, and they paid large sums to shoot civilians for fun. Many people found this story hard to believe. No strong proof was ever found; however, journalists continued to investigate. Whether or not it is true, the idea of people paying to hunt humans during war shows how cruel people can become in times of conflict. Difficult words: siege (a military attack that keeps people trapped), testify (to speak officially in court), proof (evidence). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was a big war in Bosnia in the 1990s. Sarajevo, the capital city, was in danger for four years. Snipers and bombs killed many people, and life was very hard. People were afraid to leave their homes because snipers could shoot them. John Jordan, a man from the US, went to help people in Sarajevo. He gave clothes and tools to firefighters. He worked in the city while bombs and snipers were around. In 2007, he spoke in court. He said that rich people from other countries came to Sarajevo to shoot people for fun. Jordan said that these people were from Italy, the US, Canada, and Russia, and they paid a lot of money to hunt people in Sarajevo. There is no strong proof of this, but some reporters looked into the story. It shows how war can make people do very bad things. Difficult words: sniper (a person who hides and shoots people), hunt (to kill for sport or food), proof (a fact or piece of information which shows that something exists or is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a war in Bosnia in the 1990s. Sarajevo, the capital city, is not safe. People are very scared. They do not walk in the street. Snipers shoot people. Bombs fall on homes. Life is hard in Sarajevo. A man from the US comes to help. His name is John Jordan. He gives boots and clothes to firefighters. He works in Sarajevo. He wants to help people. Later, John talks in a court . He says that rich people come to Sarajevo. They give money. They shoot people for fun. We do not know if this story is true. There is no evidence of it. But the story shows that war makes people do very bad things. Difficult words: sniper (a person who hides and shoots people), court (a place where people talk about crimes), evidence (things or information which show that something happens or is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 150 people have died in Nigeria after heavy rain caused severe flooding in the northern market town of Mokwa. The rain lasted for hours and destroyed homes, roads, and bridges. The military has been sent in to help, and the president has made the rescue efforts a top priority. Emergency teams are still searching for bodies and helping survivors. Thousands of people have lost their homes and are now in temporary shelters with limited food, clean water, and medicine. Survivors describe being stranded , losing loved ones, and fearing what will come next. Some people in Mokwa said they have received little or no help from aid agencies. The situation remains desperate, with growing concern about waterborne diseases and a lack of shelter and food. Climate experts say that while seasonal rain is common in West Africa, climate change is now making such storms much worse. They warn that extreme weather like this may become even more common in the future. Difficult words: stranded (left without the means to move from somewhere), waterborne (carried by or through water). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Heavy rain in northern Nigeria killed more than 150 people and destroyed the market town of Mokwa. The flooding started after strong rain and washed away homes, roads, and bridges. Over 5,000 people now have no homes. The army and emergency teams are trying to help, but many people say they don’t have enough food or shelter . Some people are still looking for family members who got lost in the flood. The government is sending help, but people need more. People are afraid of disease and need water, food, and shelter. Many families lost everything, and they don’t know what to do next. The rainy season is normal in West Africa, but scientists say climate change is making the rain much worse. They say that extreme weather will be more common in the future. Difficult words: shelter (a safe place to stay), common (normal, usual). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Heavy rain causes big floods in the market town of Mokwa, Nigeria. Many people die. Water destroys many homes. The water is very high, and people lose everything. They do not have food, clothes, and homes. More than 150 people die, and many more have no place to sleep now. The army and rescue workers are helping. Some people are still missing. People are scared. They need food, water, and a safe place to stay. Some help comes, but it is not enough yet. Many people are still waiting for help. The rain is part of the rainy season , but now the storms are worse. Scientists say that this is because of climate change. Difficult words: flood (a lot of water in streets and homes), destroy (to damage something so badly that you cannot use it anymore), rescue worker (a person whose job is to save someone from danger), rainy season (the time of year when a lot of rain falls in some tropical regions of the world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new neighborhood called Dixon Trail in Escondido, near San Diego, has been built with special protection against wildfires. It is the first in the US to meet and go beyond California’s building rules for high-risk fire zones. The project was developed by KB Homes and the Insurance Institute for Business and Home Safety. Every house in this area is designed to stop fires from spreading, even from wind-blown embers that can travel long distances. To achieve this, the builders used fire-resistant materials on the outside of the houses. For example, the garage doors and front doors are made of metal, and even the window shutters are covered with material that can’t burn. These features help stop fires from starting or entering homes through small gaps. Wildfires in California have destroyed many neighborhoods in recent years. That’s why the builders wanted a community solution, not just individual homes, to increase safety and help protect lives and property. Difficult words: ember (a small glowing piece of burning material), feature (a typical quality or an important part of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new neighborhood in Escondido, near San Diego, has strong protection from wildfires. It is the first place in the US built with better safety than what the state rules ask for. KB Homes and a safety group worked together to make this happen. All the houses are built to stop the fire from spreading, even when the wind carries small burning pieces. The builders used strong and safe materials. The garage and front doors are metal, and the shutters are covered with special materials. These things stop the fire from starting or getting into the homes. Wildfires destroy many homes in California. That is why the builders wanted to protect the whole neighborhood, not just one house. This plan helps make people and their homes safer. Difficult words: protection (keeping someone or something safe from injury, damage, or loss), safety (being safe), shutter (a cover for windows). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a new place in California. The name is Dixon Trail. It is close to San Diego. People build this place to be safe from fire. The houses stop the fire from coming in. The builders use strong materials which do not burn. The doors are metal. The windows have shutters . These shutters stop the fire from getting inside. The wind cannot bring fire into the homes. Many fires happen in California. Fires burn many homes. Now, builders make new and safe homes. This new place is for many people. All the homes are strong. It is not just one house. It is a safe place for all. Difficult words: metal (a hard, strong material), shutter (a cover for windows). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new statue of Josef Stalin has been placed in a Moscow Metro station, showing how Russia is changing the way it remembers its past. After his death, Stalin’s statues were removed, and his crimes were condemned . But recently, Stalin has been shown again as a strong leader and wartime hero. Some young people even believe he is unfairly hated and support his role in Russian history. Stalin is not the only thing coming back. An adviser to President Putin recently claimed that the Soviet Union still exists due to legal mistakes during its collapse. This idea is supported by other politicians and nationalists . They use it to argue that the war in Ukraine is not a foreign war but an internal Russian issue. This is part of a wider movement in Russia. Leaders are changing how people see the past to support current actions, like the war and tensions with the West. They reinterpret history to build a new national story. Difficult words: condemn (to say something is bad or wrong), nationalist (a person who strongly identifies with their nation and supports its interests), reinterpret (to understand something in a new or different way). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Moscow, people have put a new statue of Josef Stalin in the Metro. In the past, Russia removed his statues because of the many people who died when he was in power. Now, the government shows him as a strong leader and the winner of the war. Some young people also say he helped the country. President Putin’s adviser says the Soviet Union still exists because its end had some legal mistakes. Some politicians and groups agree, and they say the war in Ukraine is not a war between two countries but a problem inside Russia. Many people in Russia are changing how they think about the past. It helps the government explain what is happening now, like the war and problems with the West. Difficult words: remove (to take away), adviser (a person who gives help or ideas to a leader), legal (about the law). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a new statue of Stalin in the Metro in Moscow. In the past, people take down his statues. Now, the government shows him as a strong man. Some young people say Stalin is a good person for the country. One man who helps President Putin says that the Soviet Union still exists . He says that the Soviet Union ends with a legal mistake. Some people say that the war in Ukraine is not a war. They say it is a problem in Russia. Many people now see the past in a new way. The government wants people to think this way. This helps them with war and problems with the West. They use the past to help today’s situation. Difficult words: statue (a big stone or metal figure), exist (to live, be), legal (about the rules of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

France’s National Assembly has voted in favor of a new bill that would allow adults with incurable illnesses to choose assisted dying. The vote passed with 305 lawmakers supporting it and 199 against. The bill will now move to the Senate for more discussion, but it could take months before a final vote is made. Assisted dying would be possible only under strict conditions. The patient must be over 18, be French or live in France, and have an advanced illness that causes severe pain and cannot be treated. The request must come from the patient and be confirmed after a time of reflection . Only those who physically cannot take the medication themselves would receive help from a doctor or nurse. Another law about palliative care , which aims to reduce pain and protect patient dignity, was also passed. Support for end-of-life options has increased in France in recent years, though debate continues, and some activists believe the legal process is too slow. Difficult words: incurable (a disease that cannot be cured), reflection (a short time to think carefully before making a decision), palliative care (care that helps with pain but doesn’t cure an illness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In France, the National Assembly agreed on a new rule which says that people with incurable illnesses can ask to take medicine that ends their life. The vote had 305 people in favor and 199 against. Now, the Senate will look at the rule which may take a long time. Only people over 18, living in France, and with strong pain that cannot be treated can ask for this medicine. They must ask on their own and confirm it after some time. If they cannot take the medicine alone, a doctor or nurse can help. The parliament also accepted a rule about palliative care which helps very ill people who have big pain. Many people in France support these changes, but some say the process is too slow. Difficult words: incurable (a disease which doctors cannot cure), in favor (to agree with or support something), treated (when someone gets care or medicine to feel better). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

France has a new rule for very sick people. They can ask for special medicine . This medicine can help them die. People must be 18 or older. They must live in France. They must feel pain . A court in Germany has ended a long-running legal case about climate change. A farmer from Peru, Saul Luciano Lliuya, tried to sue the German company RWE. He said RWE had produced greenhouse gases, causing a glacier near his town to melt. He wanted the company to help protect his home. RWE replied that it had never worked in Peru and that climate change is a global issue, not a local one. Finally, the court said there was not enough risk to the farmer’s house to continue the case. Because of that, they said the case couldn’t move forward, and the decision was final . It ended a case that had lasted for nearly ten years. Even though the court rejected this lawsuit , it also said big companies should be responsible for their emissions and the global warming they cause. Experts believe this case will influence similar climate lawsuits in other countries, such as the USA, Indonesia, and Belgium. It could help future courts decide if companies should pay for climate damage. Difficult words: final (the last, coming at the end), lawsuit (a legal court case). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A farmer from Peru said a German company, RWE, caused a lot of pollution . He said this made a glacier near his town melt. He wanted the company to pay money to help his town. The company said it didn’t work in Peru. It said climate change is a global problem. A court in Germany looked at the case and said the farmer’s house was not in real danger. Because of that, the case couldn’t continue. The case is now over, and there is nothing the farmer can do. On the other hand, the court also said that companies like RWE should take care of their actions. Some people say this case is still important. It could help people in other countries take big companies to court for climate problems. Difficult words: pollution (dirty air or water), glacier (big ice that moves slowly), global (about the whole world, not just one country or place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: glacier (big ice which moves slowly), melt (when ice or snow turns into water), over (finished, not happening anymore). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Cameroon is preparing for presidential elections in October, while a violent conflict continues in its two English-speaking regions. This conflict started in 2016 after peaceful protests against discrimination turned into a crisis. The government responded with force, leading to violent clashes between Cameroonian troops and separatists who want to create a new country called Ambazonia. The conflict has caused the deaths of over 6,000 people and forced hundreds of thousands to leave their homes. Schools, businesses, and families have suffered greatly. The separatists have attacked people they see as supporting the government. This includes civil servants and workers of state-run companies. Some have been kidnapped or killed. At the same time, government forces have been accused of serious human rights abuses like torture, rape, and burning villages. Both sides have tried to silence journalists reporting on the crisis, making it hard to know what is really happening. Even after several peace efforts, the situation remains very unstable. Many people are still suffering and afraid, with no clear end in sight. Difficult words: discrimination (unfair treatment of people), separatist (a person who wants a region to become independent), civil servant (a person who works in a department of a country’s government). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Cameroon will have elections in October, but a war is still happening in the English-speaking areas. This war started in 2016 after people protested because they felt treated badly. The situation has a bad impact on workers and schools. Some people are missing. The army and the fighters both do bad things. Journalists find it hard to work because they are not safe. Peace talks didn’t change anything. The people in the area still live in fear. It is not clear when this war will stop. Difficult words: treated (how others help you or speak about you), violent (using force to hurt people or break things), peace talk (a meeting to try to stop a war or fighting). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A Norwegian man, Johan Helberg, had a surprising experience when he woke up to find a massive cargo ship just meters from his house. The 135-meter-long ship, called NCL Salten, had run aground early in the morning near his home along the Trondheim Fjord. Johan was unaware of the event until his neighbor rang his doorbell to inform him. He later told reporters that he slept through the whole incident, and luckily, the only damage was a wire connected to his heating pump. Helberg described the moment as unforgettable and said he wouldn’t trade it for anything. Pictures show the ship’s large red and green bow extremely close to his house. Authorities confirmed that no one was injured, and no oil spilled from the ship. However, efforts to move the ship during high tide were unsuccessful. The shipping company said they are helping with the investigation, and police say there is one suspect, although they haven’t released more details yet. Difficult words: massive (very large), unaware (not knowing something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Johan Helberg from Norway had a big surprise one morning. A large ship came onto the land and stopped very close to his house. The ship is 135 meters long and ran aground early in the morning. Johan didn’t hear anything and was still sleeping. His neighbor rang the doorbell to tell him what happened. Johan said the moment was strange, but he also felt lucky. The ship didn’t crash into the house, but it broke one wire on the heating pump. Nobody got hurt, and no oil came out of the ship. The police and the shipping company are checking what happened. They tried to move the ship back into the water, but it didn’t work. Police said they are looking into one person who probably made a mistake. The shipping company said they were helping the police with the case. Difficult words: surprise (something you don’t expect), run aground (when a boat or ship goes onto land or shallow water and cannot move), probably (very likely, but not sure). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Real Madrid has announced that Xabi Alonso will become their new head coach for the next three seasons until June 2028. Alonso is a legendary former player who represented the club between 2009 and 2014, playing in 236 official matches and winning six major titles. He was also an important part of the Spanish national team, winning the World Cup in 2010 and two European Championships. After finishing his career as a player, Alonso started coaching in Real Madrid’s academy. Later, he managed Bayer Leverkusen in Germany, where he was very successful. His team went through the domestic season without losing a game and won two big trophies. They lost the Europa League final to Atalanta, but the season was still considered a big success. Alonso will be officially presented as Real Madrid’s new coach at a special event. The club president will welcome him, and he will speak to the media. The team hopes he can bring more titles to the club as a coach. Difficult words: legendary (very famous and respected), domestic (related to one’s own country). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In its latest issue, Bon Appétit magazine has created a special theme that mixes food with art. The magazine has introduced recipes that are inspired by famous artworks. For example, a painting by abstract artist Helen Frankenthaler has been turned into a falafel burger with chickpea patties and pickled onions. A minimalist work by Agnes Martin became a dish of scallops with lemon-flavored spinach sauce. A colorful piece by feminist artist Judy Chicago was transformed into a salad of radishes and soft-boiled eggs. These recipes aim to reflect the spirit and colors of the original artworks through carefully chosen ingredients and presentation. One dessert tribute includes a cake inspired by Wayne Thiebaud’s painting Cake Slice. The dessert includes layers of vanilla, chocolate, and strawberry cake with sour cream frosting. These artistic recipes date back to artworks from as early as 1959, just a few years after Bon Appétit began publishing. This creative idea brings together visual art and culinary design in a unique and fun way. Difficult words: scallop (soft round seafood), culinary (related to cooking or the kitchen). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

It looks like a painting by artist Wayne Thiebaud. The cake also has sour cream frosting. These dishes are not only for eating but also for enjoying art. The magazine wants people to see food in a new way. The paintings are from around 1959, a few years after Bon Appétit began. Difficult words: falafel (small round balls made from herbs and chickpeas), chickpeas (a small bean), scallop (a kind of seafood). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Talks between Iran and the United States restarted in Rome, Italy, to resolve long-standing disagreements about Iran’s nuclear program. Iran’s Foreign Minister and Trump’s Middle East envoy are leading the fifth round of discussions. While the US wants to stop Iran from creating a nuclear weapon, Iran wants relief from economic sanctions. The situation is tense, and both sides have stated strong conditions for any agreement. Iran’s nuclear program is moving quickly, and experts say Iran could soon have enough enriched uranium for a bomb. However, it is not certain whether Iran has the technical knowledge to build one. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) can’t fully inspect Iran’s nuclear sites anymore, which increases global concern and makes the current talks in Rome even more important. The US hopes for a peaceful solution but demands Iran stop supporting terrorism and end its nuclear ambitions . Although both sides are still negotiating, Iran’s supreme leader is final in any decision. Difficult words: envoy (a person who is sent by one government to talk to another government), enriched uranium (a type of uranium that has been changed to make it more powerful), ambition (a strong desire to do or achieve something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Iran and the US are talking in Rome, Italy, about Iran’s nuclear plans. This is the fifth time they met. The US wants Iran to stop trying to make a nuclear weapon. Iran wants the US to remove economic sanctions. Iran is now making nuclear material very fast, and experts think it could have enough material for a bomb in just a few weeks. The group that checks nuclear sites, the IAEA, cannot visit all the places in Iran anymore, which makes other countries very worried. The US wants to find a peaceful way to stop Iran, but Iran’s top leader has the final word. Even though Iran’s government is doing the talking, the leader controls what they can agree to, making everything more difficult. Difficult words: nuclear (using energy from atoms), remove (to take away), peaceful (calm). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US wants peace . Iran’s top leader is very important. He says yes or no. The people in the talks cannot say yes without him. He has the final word, which makes the talks slow and hard. Difficult words: nuclear (energy from small parts of atoms), sanction (money or rules which punish a country), peace (time without a war or fight), final (last). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Gaza, the sound of drones is constant . Al Jazeera’s Sanad team found that Israel is using DJI drones, originally made for civilian purposes, in military operations. These drones, often used by farmers or filmmakers, are now being used for surveillance , tunnel searches, and even bombing. Some drones, like the Agras model, were built to spray crops but have been modified to drop explosives on homes, schools, and hospitals. Footage confirmed by Sanad shows several attacks using these repurposed drones, including strikes near shelters and hospitals in Gaza. In one case, a drone dropped a bomb just 100 meters from a school. Another drone was seen tracking a man and making him open doors while soldiers followed. People say they had to flee again because of drone strikes. Although DJI stopped selling drones to Russia and Ukraine in 2022, they still sell to Israel. DJI says its drones are for peaceful use and that Israel has no special access, but many are concerned about how these drones are being used in war. Difficult words: constant (happening all the time, without stopping), surveillance (watching people or places closely), repurposed (changed to be used in a different way than it was made for). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Some videos show drones bombing areas near a hospital and a school. In one video, a drone followed a man. Soldiers made him open doors inside a school. People had to leave their homes again because of drone attacks. DJI said its drones are not for war. The company stopped selling drones to Russia and Ukraine but still sells them to Israel. This makes many people feel afraid. Difficult words: drone (a small flying machine), drop (to let something fall). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Henry is a tour guide working in central London who has ADHD, which stands for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. This condition makes it hard for him to do everyday tasks, like remembering appointments, sorting laundry, or even getting ready on time. Henry describes his brain as a tombola, a game where many random balls come out, representing thoughts and reminders he must manage. Sometimes the constant noise and instructions in his head overwhelm him, causing frustration and feelings of shame. He explains how this can make him feel like he is fighting his brain every day, struggling with even basic tasks. Despite these difficulties, Henry embraces his ADHD and says he doesn’t need fixing. His family understands the emotional challenges he faces and supports him with love. By sharing his story, Henry hopes to help others understand that ADHD affects many parts of life, not just school, and that living with it means taking some detours but still moving forward. Difficult words: constant (never stopping), embrace (to accept fully), detour (a different path from the usual way). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
